Title: LANDFALL: New Android Spyware Targeting Samsung Devices

Victim.Description: The victims are users of Samsung Galaxy devices, primarily located in the Middle East.

diamond_model_summary: The LANDFALL incident involves a sophisticated adversary using advanced capabilities to exploit zero-day vulnerabilities in Samsung devices. The infrastructure includes multiple C2 servers, and the victims are primarily Samsung Galaxy users in the Middle East. The adversary's strategic objective is espionage and data exfiltration, employing TTPs like zero-click exploits and malformed DNG files.
doc_summary: Unit 42 researchers discovered a new Android spyware family named LANDFALL, targeting Samsung Galaxy devices through a zero-day vulnerability (CVE-2025-21042) in Samsung's image processing library. The spyware was delivered via malformed DNG image files, likely sent through WhatsApp, and enabled comprehensive surveillance, including microphone recording and location tracking. Title: Malicious NuGet Packages Targeting .NET Applications and Siemens S7 PLCs

Victim.Description: Victims include developers and organizations using .NET applications and Siemens S7 PLCs.
Victim.Security_Posture: Compromised if malicious packages are present

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves an adversary using the developer name 'shanhai666' to distribute malicious packages on NuGet, targeting .NET applications and Siemens S7 PLCs. The adversary's capability includes using legitimate code to obfuscate malicious payloads, with a focus on disrupting database and industrial control operations. The infrastructure leverages NuGet as a distribution platform, and the victims are developers and organizations using .NET and Siemens S7 PLCs.
doc_summary: Several malicious packages on NuGet have been discovered with sabotage payloads scheduled to activate in 2027 and 2028, targeting database implementations and Siemens S7 industrial control devices. The malicious code uses a probabilistic trigger, potentially activating based on parameters on the infected device. NuGet, an open-source package manager, allows developers to download .NET libraries. Researchers at Socket found nine malicious packages on NuGet, published under the developer name 'shanhai666', featuring legitimate functionality alongside harmful code. These packages target major database providers used in .NET applications, including SQL Server, PostgreSQL, and SQLite. The most dangerous package, Sharp7Extend, targets users of the legitimate Sharp7 library for Siemens PLCs. The threat actor exploits developers searching for Sharp7 extensions by appending 'Extend' to the trusted name. The packages contain mostly legitimate code, creating a false sense of safety, but include a small malicious payload. The malware exploits C# extension methods to inject malicious logic into database and PLC operations. A verification for the current date against a hardcoded trigger date determines activation. If conditions are met, the code may terminate the host process or corrupt PLC writes, leading to operational disruptions. Organizations are advised to audit their assets for these packages and assume compromise if present.
kill_chain_summary: The adversary conducted reconnaissance to identify popular .NET libraries and Siemens S7 PLCs, weaponized legitimate libraries by appending malicious code, and delivered these packages through NuGet. The exploitation phase involves using C# extension methods to inject harmful logic, while installation occurs as the packages are added as dependencies. The actions on objectives include disrupting operations through process termination and data corruption.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of legitimate tools like NuGet and Sharp7Extend, with TTPs involving the obfuscation of malicious payloads and probabilistic activation triggers. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domains were identified, making detection challenging. The adversary's tactics focus on disrupting operations through sophisticated multi-layered attacks.

doc_summary: A zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2025-21042, in Samsung Galaxy Android devices was exploited to deliver LANDFALL spyware in targeted attacks in the Middle East. The flaw, an out-of-bounds write in libimagecodec.quram.so, allowed remote code execution. The attacks, tracked as CL-UNK-1054, targeted Iraq, Iran, Turkey, and Morocco. LANDFALL, a comprehensive spy tool, harvested sensitive data using a zero-click exploit via malicious DNG files sent over WhatsApp. The spyware communicated with a C2 server, potentially linked to Stealth Falcon. Samsung patched the flaw in April 2025.

doc_summary: Microsoft security researchers discovered a new backdoor malware named SesameOp, which uses the OpenAI Assistants API as a covert command-and-control channel. The malware was identified during an investigation into a July 2025 cyberattack. SesameOp allows attackers to gain persistent access to compromised environments and manage backdoored devices remotely by leveraging legitimate cloud services. The malware uses the OpenAI Assistants API to fetch compressed and encrypted commands, which are then decrypted and executed on infected systems. The attack chain involved a heavily obfuscated loader and a .NET-based backdoor deployed into multiple Microsoft Visual Studio utilities. Microsoft and OpenAI collaborated to investigate the threat actors' abuse of the API, leading to the identification and disabling of the account and API key used in the attacks. To mitigate the impact, Microsoft advises auditing firewall logs, enabling tamper protection, configuring endpoint detection in block mode, and monitoring unauthorized connections to external services.
kill_chain_summary: The SesameOp attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with the installation of a .NET-based backdoor into Microsoft Visual Studio utilities. The command-and-control stage is executed through the OpenAI Assistants API, allowing the adversary to maintain persistence and conduct espionage. Actions on objectives include data collection and exfiltration, with the adversary leveraging legitimate cloud services to avoid detection.

Title: Malicious NuGet Packages Targeting Industrial Control Systems

Victim.Description: The victims are developers and organizations using NuGet packages, particularly those in manufacturing environments.

diamond_model_summary: The Diamond Model analysis reveals a sophisticated adversary, 'shanhai666', suspected to be of Chinese origin, targeting industrial control systems through malicious NuGet packages. The adversary's capability includes embedding time-delayed payloads in software dependencies, exploiting C# extension methods to execute sabotage. The infrastructure involves the distribution of these packages via the NuGet repository, affecting manufacturing environments. Victims are developers and organizations using these packages, with a high impact on operational data and database integrity.
doc_summary: A sophisticated supply chain attack involving nine malicious NuGet packages was identified, targeting industrial control systems and databases. Published by a user named 'shanhai666', these packages are designed to execute time-delayed payloads, with trigger dates set for August 2027 and November 2028. The most dangerous package, Sharp7Extend, targets Siemens S7 PLCs, causing random process terminations and silent write failures. The attack leverages C# extension methods to inject malicious code, affecting SQL Server, PostgreSQL, and SQLite implementations. The threat actor's origin is suspected to be China, and the campaign demonstrates advanced techniques in software supply chain attacks.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain analysis identifies multiple stages in the attack. Reconnaissance likely involved identifying target environments and suitable packages. Weaponization was achieved by embedding malicious code in NuGet packages. Delivery occurred through the NuGet repository, targeting developers. Exploitation involved executing malicious code via C# extension methods. Installation was achieved by integrating the packages as dependencies. Actions on objectives included sabotaging industrial control systems and databases through time-delayed payloads. The attack demonstrates advanced techniques in software supply chain attacks.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain analysis highlights the difficulty in detecting and responding to this attack. The use of time-delayed payloads and probabilistic execution makes it challenging to identify specific indicators such as hashes, IPs, or domains. The adversary's use of C# extension methods and malicious NuGet packages represents a high level of sophistication, complicating detection and remediation efforts. The attack's impact on industrial control systems and databases underscores the need for robust supply chain security measures.

Title: Operation Chargeback: Dismantling of Credit Card Fraud Networks

Victim.Description: Victims were credit card holders across 193 countries, defrauded through unauthorized transactions.

diamond_model_summary: Operation Chargeback involved dismantling three major credit card fraud and money laundering networks. The adversaries were organized criminal groups exploiting payment service infrastructures to defraud millions of cardholders globally. The operation was a coordinated effort by international law enforcement agencies, highlighting the importance of cross-border cooperation in tackling complex financial crimes.
doc_summary: International authorities dismantled three massive credit card fraud and money laundering networks linked to losses exceeding €300 million, affecting over 4.3 million cardholders across 193 countries. The operation, dubbed 'Operation Chargeback', involved investigators from Germany, the United States, Canada, Singapore, Luxembourg, Cyprus, Spain, Italy, and the Netherlands. Led by German prosecutors and the Federal Criminal Police Office, and coordinated by Eurojust and Europol, the operation targeted 44 suspects, resulting in the arrest of 18 individuals, including executives from major German payment service providers. The fraud involved creating fake online subscriptions using stolen credit card data, facilitated by shell companies in the United Kingdom and Cyprus. The suspects exploited the infrastructure of German payment service providers to process and launder illicit transactions.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for Operation Chargeback involved several stages, including reconnaissance to identify vulnerable payment service providers, weaponization through the use of stolen credit card data, and delivery by processing unauthorized transactions. Exploitation involved using the payment infrastructure to facilitate fraud, while installation included setting up fake subscriptions. The operation's success underscores the need for robust detection and remediation strategies to prevent similar incidents.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: Operation Chargeback did not reveal specific indicators such as hashes, IP addresses, or domains, making it challenging to populate the Pyramid of Pain. The operation focused on dismantling the infrastructure and arresting key individuals involved in the fraud networks. This highlights the importance of targeting the adversary's infrastructure and operational capabilities to disrupt their activities effectively.

doc_summary: Sarah from accounting received a phishing email disguised as a password reset from the organization's cloud provider. She unknowingly provided her credentials to cybercriminals, who sell such information on dark web marketplaces. The credential theft ecosystem involves various actors, including opportunistic fraudsters, automated botnets, and organized crime groups. These actors exploit stolen credentials for financial gain, network mapping, and large-scale attacks. Organizations face regulatory fines, lawsuits, and reputational damage from such incidents. Tools like Outpost24's Credential Checker help identify compromised credentials. The incident highlights the importance of detecting and remediating credential compromises promptly.

doc_summary: Google has introduced a form for businesses on Google Maps to report extortion attempts by threat actors posting fake negative reviews. This practice, known as review bombing, involves bad actors flooding a business's profile with fake one-star reviews and then contacting the business owner to demand payment for their removal. The threat actors use third-party messaging apps to communicate and warn of further escalation if the ransom is not paid, potentially damaging the business's public rating and reputation. Google advises users to be cautious of unexpected delivery texts or emails demanding fees, and to download apps only from trusted sources. The development coincides with a report from Reuters about Meta's revenue from scam ads, highlighting the prevalence of online scams.

Access_Vectors: Remote code execution via eval injection
Victim.Description: Organizations using XWiki Platform, particularly those with guest access enabled.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical vulnerability in the XWiki Platform, identified as CVE-2025-24893, which allows unauthenticated remote code execution via an eval injection flaw. The vulnerability is particularly dangerous due to its accessibility to guest users, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary commands and potentially compromise sensitive data. CISA has issued guidance for remediation, emphasizing the need for immediate patching and network segmentation to mitigate risks.
doc_summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has identified a critical vulnerability in the XWiki Platform, designated as CVE-2025-24893, which allows unauthenticated remote code execution via an eval injection flaw in the SolrSearch component. This vulnerability, classified under CWE-95, poses a severe risk to organizations using XWiki, as it can be exploited by guest users to execute arbitrary commands, potentially compromising sensitive data and enabling further attacks. CISA has issued guidance for remediation by November 20, 2025, recommending immediate application of security patches and adherence to Binding Operational Directive 22-01 for cloud-based instances. Organizations are advised to assess their XWiki deployments, contact XWiki support for patch information, and implement network segmentation to mitigate potential lateral movement.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves reconnaissance to identify vulnerable XWiki instances, weaponization through crafting of malicious requests, delivery via sending these requests to the target, and exploitation through execution of arbitrary code. While no specific installation or command and control activities are detected, potential actions on objectives include data theft and lateral movement. Organizations are advised to apply patches and implement network segmentation to prevent exploitation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is primarily focused on the TTPs associated with the eval injection vulnerability in XWiki Platform. No specific hash values, IP addresses, or domain names are identified, but the exploit of CVE-2025-24893 represents a significant threat. Organizations should prioritize patching and network segmentation to mitigate the risk of exploitation.

doc_summary: Security researchers at the SANS Internet Storm Center detected a spike in suspicious network traffic targeting Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) infrastructure worldwide. The activity focuses on TCP ports 8530 and 8531, linked to CVE-2025-59287, a critical vulnerability in WSUS servers. Attackers exploit this flaw to execute arbitrary scripts, gaining control over systems and potentially distributing malicious patches. Data from firewall sensors confirmed increased scanning attempts, with some originating from known research sources like Shadowserver. However, unauthorized IP addresses indicate genuine threat actor reconnaissance. Johannes Ullrich from SANS.edu warns that exposed WSUS servers should be considered compromised. Organizations must urgently patch vulnerable systems or implement network segmentation to mitigate risks.

The incident highlights the need for immediate patching and network segmentation to mitigate risks.

Victim.Description: Organizations using Ubiquiti's UniFi Dream Machine routers and access control systems.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to misconfigured API endpoints.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a critical RCE vulnerability in Ubiquiti's UniFi OS, allowing adversaries to gain unauthorized access and control over devices. The adversary exploited a misconfigured API endpoint, leading to command injection and full system access. The infrastructure targeted includes UniFi Dream Machine routers and access control systems, posing significant risks to organizations using these devices.
doc_summary: Security researchers discovered a critical unauthenticated Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerability in Ubiquiti's UniFi OS, tracked as CVE-2025-52665. This flaw allows attackers to gain full control of UniFi devices, including Dream Machine routers and access control systems, without credentials. The vulnerability originates from a misconfigured backup API endpoint at /api/ucore/backup/export, accessible externally through port 9780. Improper input validation on the dir parameter allows command injection, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary commands. Researchers demonstrated the severity by exfiltrating the /etc/passwd file and establishing a reverse shell. Additional unauthenticated API endpoints were found, exposing sensitive credential material and allowing manipulation of access control systems. The vulnerability poses significant risks to organizations using UniFi devices.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with the exploitation of a misconfigured API endpoint in Ubiquiti's UniFi OS. The adversary leveraged command injection to gain initial access, followed by establishing a reverse shell for command and control. The final stage involved actions on objectives, including exfiltration of sensitive files and manipulation of access control systems.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes TTPs such as command injection and exploitation of unauthenticated API endpoints. doc_summary: Apple released security updates for iOS 26.1 and iPadOS 26.1 on November 3, 2025, addressing multiple vulnerabilities. These updates are available for iPhone 11 and later, and various iPad models. Key fixes include vulnerabilities in the Apple Neural Engine (CVE-2025-43447, CVE-2025-43462) that could cause system crashes or kernel memory corruption, and the Apple Account feature (CVE-2025-43455) that allowed malicious apps to capture screenshots of private information. WebKit, the browser engine for Safari, had several critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2025-43438, CVE-2025-43433, CVE-2025-43421) leading to memory corruption and unsafe data leaks. AppleMobileFileIntegrity and Assets components were updated to prevent sandbox escapes (CVE-2025-43379, CVE-2025-43407). Privacy issues in Control Center (CVE-2025-43350) and Status Bar (CVE-2025-43460) were also addressed. Apple advises users to install these updates promptly to mitigate risks.
kill_chain_summary: The vulnerabilities in Apple's iOS and iPadOS represent potential exploitation points in the kill chain. Apple's updates aim to mitigate these risks by improving memory management and input validation.

doc_summary: A critical security vulnerability, CVE-2025-11953, was discovered in the @react-native-community/cli NPM package, affecting millions of developers using React Native. The vulnerability exists in versions 4.8.0 through 20.0.0-alpha.2 and has been patched in version 20.0.0. Developers are advised to update to the patched version or mitigate by binding the server to localhost. The infrastructure at risk includes Linux-based web servers and hosting environments using Control Web Panel. The victim profile is broad, affecting any organization using this server management platform. The severity of the impact is critical, with potential unauthorized access to sensitive data.
doc_summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has issued an urgent alert regarding a critical command-injection vulnerability in Control Web Panel, tracked as CVE-2025-48703. This flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary operating system commands remotely, potentially leading to complete server compromise and unauthorized access to sensitive data. The vulnerability exists in the file manager module of Control Web Panel and affects how the application handles the t_total parameter in changePerm requests. Attackers can inject shell metacharacters into this parameter to bypass input validation. The flaw is classified as CWE-78, improper neutralization of special elements in an OS command. CISA recommends immediate application of vendor-provided security patches and mitigations, with a mandatory response deadline of November 25, 2025. Organizations unable to patch systems immediately should implement network-level controls to restrict access to the vulnerable application.

doc_summary: The Django development team released critical security patches on November 5, 2025, addressing two significant vulnerabilities: a high-severity SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2025-64459) affecting QuerySet operations and a moderate-severity denial-of-service vulnerability (CVE-2025-64458) impacting Windows-based installations. The SQL injection flaw allows attackers to inject malicious SQL commands into database queries via the QuerySet.filter(), QuerySet.exclude(), and QuerySet.get() methods, as well as the Q() class, when using a specially crafted dictionary with dictionary expansion as the _connector argument. The denial-of-service vulnerability involves inefficient NFKC Unicode normalization processing in Python, which can be exploited by sending requests with excessive Unicode data, causing resource exhaustion. Patches have been applied to Django versions 5.2.8, 5.1.14, and 4.2.26, and organizations are urged to update immediately.

doc_summary: Cisco has issued a critical security advisory for two severe vulnerabilities in its Unified Contact Center Express (CCX) platform, identified as CVE-2025-20354 and CVE-2025-20358. These vulnerabilities, published on November 5, 2025, allow remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands and gain unauthorized system access. doc_summary: Cisco has issued a critical warning about ongoing attacks targeting a severe remote code execution vulnerability affecting its Secure Firewall, Adaptive Security Appliance, and Threat Defense Software. The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2025-20333, affects the VPN web server component in both Cisco Secure ASA and Secure FTD firewall platforms. An authenticated remote attacker can exploit improper input validation in HTTP requests to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on affected devices. This represents a significant risk for organizations relying on these firewalls for network perimeter defense, as successful exploitation could allow attackers to bypass all security controls. Cisco became aware of a new attack variant in early November that specifically targets devices running vulnerable versions of ASA and FTD software. This variant causes unpatched devices to reload, creating denial-of-service conditions that disrupt network operations unexpectedly. The vulnerability requires valid VPN user credentials to exploit, meaning attackers must first obtain legitimate authentication details through phishing, credential theft, or insider threats. Organizations running Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software or Secure FTD Software with VPN features enabled face immediate risk. Vulnerable configurations include AnyConnect IKEv2 Remote Access with client services, Mobile User Security implementations, and SSL VPN deployments. The attack’s ability to achieve complete device compromise makes this particularly concerning, as attackers could modify firewall rules, redirect traffic, or establish persistent backdoors. Cisco has released fixed software versions and strongly recommends all customers upgrade immediately. No workarounds are available to mitigate this vulnerability, leaving patching as the only viable remediation.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable Cisco devices, followed by exploitation of CVE-2025-20333 to gain initial access. The exploitation stage involves executing arbitrary code with root privileges, potentially leading to the installation of backdoors for persistence. Title: SleepyDuck Remote Access Trojan in Open VSX Registry

Victim.Description: Developers using the Open VSX registry for VS Code extensions.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable due to reliance on community-driven extension registry

diamond_model_summary: The SleepyDuck incident involves an adversary targeting developers using the Open VSX registry by embedding a remote access trojan in a seemingly legitimate Solidity extension. The adversary's capability includes using Ethereum smart contracts for command-and-control communication, ensuring persistence and redundancy. The infrastructure leverages the Open VSX registry for distribution and the Ethereum blockchain for C2 communication. Victims are primarily developers in the software development industry, with their environments and potentially sensitive data at risk.
doc_summary: The SleepyDuck remote access trojan, disguised as a Solidity extension in the Open VSX registry, uses an Ethereum smart contract for command-and-control communication. The extension, 'juan-bianco.solidity-vlang', was initially harmless but gained malicious capabilities after an update. It has been downloaded over 53,000 times. The malware activates on editor startup, collects system data, and uses Ethereum for C2 redundancy. Open VSX's popularity has made it a target for malicious submissions. Secure Annex reported on the malware's use of Ethereum contracts to update C2 server addresses, ensuring long-term persistence. Developers are advised to download extensions from reputable sources.
kill_chain_summary: The SleepyDuck attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify popular platforms and extensions. Weaponization involved embedding the RAT in a legitimate-looking extension. Delivery occurred through the Open VSX registry, exploiting the VS Code environment for execution. Installation was achieved by activating the RAT upon opening a Solidity file. Command and control were maintained via Ethereum smart contracts, allowing the adversary to collect system data and execute commands. The attack highlights the need for vigilance in downloading extensions from trusted sources.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The SleepyDuck incident presents challenges in detection and response due to its use of Ethereum smart contracts for command-and-control communication. Traditional indicators such as IP addresses and domain names are absent, complicating detection efforts. The reliance on blockchain technology for C2 redundancy increases the difficulty of disrupting the attack. This incident underscores the importance of monitoring for behavioral indicators and maintaining robust security practices to mitigate the impact of such sophisticated threats.

Title: European Law Enforcement Arrests Cryptocurrency Fraud Network

Victim.Description: Individuals across multiple countries targeted by fake investment platforms.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a sophisticated adversary group that created fake cryptocurrency investment platforms to defraud victims. The adversary's capability includes using blockchain tools for laundering stolen funds. The infrastructure consists of fake websites and social media channels for recruitment. Victims are individuals across multiple countries, primarily in the financial sector.
doc_summary: European law enforcement authorities arrested nine suspected money launderers involved in a cryptocurrency fraud network that stole over €600 million from victims across multiple countries. The fraudsters created fake cryptocurrency investment platforms, promising high returns, and recruited victims through social media and cold calling. Once victims transferred their cryptocurrency, they were unable to recover their funds. The criminals laundered more than €600 million using blockchain tools. The operation took place on October 27 and 29 in Cyprus, Spain, and Germany, coordinated by Eurojust. Searches resulted in the seizure of EUR 800,000 in bank accounts, EUR 415,000 in cryptocurrencies, and EUR 300,000 in cash. The network used fake news articles and testimonials to lure victims. European police linked this to another large-scale cryptocurrency fraud network that stole over €100 million since 2018. The U.S. Federal Trade Commission reported investment scams as the highest reported losses, totaling approximately $5.7 billion.
kill_chain_summary: The adversary conducted reconnaissance through social media and cold calling to identify victims. They weaponized by creating fake investment platforms and delivered their scheme through social engineering tactics. Exploitation occurred when victims transferred cryptocurrency to these platforms. The adversary's actions on objectives involved laundering the stolen funds using blockchain tools.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is primarily focused on domain names and TTPs. The adversary's use of fake cryptocurrency platforms and social engineering tactics are key indicators. While specific hashes and IP addresses are not identified, the use of blockchain tools for laundering adds complexity to detection and response efforts.

Title: Curly COMrades Exploit Microsoft Hyper-V to Evade Detection

Victim.Description: Targets include government and judicial bodies in Georgia and energy firms in Moldova.

diamond_model_summary: Curly COMrades, a Russian hacker group, exploited Microsoft Hyper-V to create a hidden Alpine Linux VM for malware deployment, targeting government and energy sectors in Georgia and Moldova. Their sophisticated tactics included custom tools CurlyShell and CurlCat, leveraging PowerShell for persistence and evasion.
doc_summary: The Russian hacker group Curly COMrades is exploiting Microsoft Hyper-V in Windows to bypass endpoint detection and response solutions by creating a hidden Alpine Linux-based virtual machine to run malware. The group, active since mid-2024, aligns with Russian geopolitical interests and targets government and judicial bodies in Georgia and energy firms in Moldova. Bitdefender, with the help of the Georgian CERT, uncovered the group's operations, which involve enabling Hyper-V, disabling its management interface, and deploying a minimalistic Alpine Linux VM. This VM hosts custom tools, CurlyShell and CurlCat, to maintain operational stealth and communication. The attackers use PowerShell scripts for persistence and pivoting, injecting Kerberos tickets into LSASS and creating local accounts via Group Policy. The sophistication of these attacks highlights the need for monitoring abnormal Hyper-V activation, LSASS access, and PowerShell script deployment.
kill_chain_summary: The attack by Curly COMrades involved exploiting Hyper-V to deploy a hidden VM, using custom malware for stealth operations. The group maintained persistence through PowerShell scripts and Kerberos ticket injection, achieving command and control via CurlCat, and executing objectives with minimal detection.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: Curly COMrades' use of custom malware and virtualization techniques presents challenges in detection. The group's reliance on Hyper-V and PowerShell scripts for persistence and evasion highlights the need for advanced monitoring of virtualization and scripting activities to disrupt their operations.

Title: University of Pennsylvania Data Breach and Email Incident

Victim.Description: The University of Pennsylvania, including its students, alumni, and donors.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves a hacker group targeting the University of Pennsylvania, exploiting compromised credentials to access and exfiltrate data from multiple systems. The adversary's primary motivation was to obtain the university's donor database, highlighting vulnerabilities in the institution's security posture.
doc_summary: A hacker group claimed responsibility for a data breach at the University of Pennsylvania, exposing data on 1.2 million donors and internal documents. The breach involved access to multiple systems, including PennKey SSO, VPN, Salesforce, Qlik, SAP, and SharePoint. Offensive emails were sent from connect.upenn.edu, a platform hosted on Salesforce Marketing Cloud. The attackers exfiltrated personal and demographic data, including names, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers, net worth, donation history, and sensitive demographic details. The breach occurred on October 30th, with data downloads completed by October 31st. The university has reported the incident to the FBI and is working with law enforcement. The attackers stated their motivation was to access the donor database, not political, and they are not extorting the university. The incident highlights potential risks for targeted phishing and social engineering attacks against donors.
kill_chain_summary: The attack followed a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable systems, followed by credential access to exploit compromised accounts. The adversary then exfiltrated sensitive donor data and used the access to send offensive emails, demonstrating a clear objective to disrupt and extract value from the university's assets.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names and tools used in the attack. The adversary leveraged compromised credentials and Salesforce Marketing Cloud to execute their objectives. The lack of specific hashes, IPs, or TTPs limits the ability to fully populate the pyramid, but the identified elements provide insight into the attack's execution.

Title: University of Pennsylvania Email Breach Incident

Victim.Description: University of Pennsylvania, its students, and alumni.

diamond_model_summary: The incident at the University of Pennsylvania involved unknown adversaries exploiting the University's email infrastructure to send offensive emails. The adversaries' motivation appears to be ideological, aiming to criticize the University's policies and practices. The attack leveraged the Salesforce Marketing Cloud platform, indicating a potential compromise of the University's account on this platform. The victim, the University of Pennsylvania, is a higher education institution in the United States, and the incident highlights vulnerabilities in email systems and the importance of robust cybersecurity measures.
doc_summary: The University of Pennsylvania experienced a cybersecurity incident involving the distribution of offensive emails to students and alumni. The emails, sent from various University email addresses, claimed data was stolen in a breach and criticized the University's security practices and admission policies. The emails were sent via 'connect.upenn.edu', a Penn mailing list platform hosted on Salesforce Marketing Cloud. The University's Incident Response team is addressing the breach, and a banner has been added to the University's website warning about the emails. The incident highlights potential vulnerabilities in email systems and the importance of robust cybersecurity measures in higher education institutions.
kill_chain_summary: The attack on the University of Pennsylvania followed a sequence of stages typical in cyber incidents. It likely began with reconnaissance to gather email addresses and system information, followed by weaponization involving the crafting of offensive email content. The delivery stage involved sending the emails via the compromised email infrastructure. Exploitation occurred through unauthorized use of the email system, leading to the distribution of the emails. The attack's primary objective was to impact the University's reputation by disseminating offensive content.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident is limited due to the lack of specific indicators such as hashes or IP addresses. The primary indicator is the domain 'connect.upenn.edu', which was used to send the emails. The use of Salesforce Marketing Cloud as a tool is also noted. The incident underscores the challenge of detecting and mitigating email-based attacks, particularly when legitimate infrastructure is exploited.

Title: Cybercriminals Target Freight Industry with RMM Tools for Cargo Theft

Victim.Description: Freight brokers and trucking carriers targeted for cargo theft.
Victim.Geography: North America, Brazil, Mexico, India, Germany, Chile, South Africa
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable to social engineering and RMM tool installation.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves threat actors targeting the freight industry with RMM tools to hijack cargo and steal goods. The adversary uses social engineering and compromised accounts to deliver malicious links, leading to the installation of RMM tools like ScreenConnect and SimpleHelp. The infrastructure includes compromised email accounts and fraudulent freight listings. Victims are primarily in the transportation sector across multiple countries.
doc_summary: Threat actors are targeting freight brokers and trucking carriers with malicious links and emails to deploy remote monitoring and management tools (RMMs) like ScreenConnect, SimpleHelp, and others. These tools enable hijacking of cargo and theft of physical goods. The activity has been tracked since June, with campaigns delivering NetSupport and ScreenConnect since January. Proofpoint has recorded nearly two dozen campaigns since August, targeting primarily North American entities, but also observed in Brazil, Mexico, India, Germany, Chile, and South Africa. The attackers use compromised accounts to post fraudulent freight listings or hijack email threads, leading victims to malicious URLs. The goal is to install RMMs on target systems for full remote control, reconnaissance, and credential harvesting. Social engineering is used to tailor messages for urgent load negotiations. The attacks suggest insider knowledge of routes, timing, and high-value cargo types, indicating collaboration with organized crime groups.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance to gather information on freight routes and high-value cargo. Weaponization involves crafting malicious emails and links. Delivery is achieved through spearphishing emails. Exploitation occurs by hijacking email threads. Installation involves deploying RMM tools on compromised systems. Command and control is maintained through these tools, allowing for remote control and data exfiltration. Actions on objectives include hijacking cargo and stealing goods.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes tools like ScreenConnect and SimpleHelp, which are used for remote control and credential harvesting. The lack of specific IP addresses, domains, or hashes limits the ability to score higher on the pyramid. The focus is on the tools and TTPs employed by the adversary, which are critical for understanding and mitigating the threat.

Title: Exploitation of CVE-2023-20198 in Cisco IOS XE Devices by BadCandy Webshell

Victim.Description: Telecommunications sector in Australia targeted by state-sponsored actors.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves state-sponsored actors, specifically the group known as Salt Typhoon, exploiting a critical vulnerability (CVE-2023-20198) in Cisco IOS XE devices. The adversaries use the BadCandy webshell to gain administrative access and execute commands with root privileges. The infrastructure targeted includes routers within the telecommunications sector in Australia, highlighting the high exposure potential due to unpatched devices. The attack demonstrates a high level of sophistication and motivation for espionage and disruption.
doc_summary: The Australian government has issued warnings about ongoing cyberattacks targeting unpatched Cisco IOS XE devices, exploiting the CVE-2023-20198 vulnerability. This critical flaw allows remote unauthenticated attackers to create a local admin user via the web interface, leading to device takeover. The BadCandy webshell, a Lua-based malware, is used to execute commands with root privileges on compromised routers. Despite Cisco's patch release in October 2023, many devices remain vulnerable, leading to continued exploitation through 2024 and 2025. The Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) has identified over 400 potentially compromised devices, with 150 still affected as of late October 2025. The attacks are attributed to state-sponsored actors, including the Chinese group Salt Typhoon, known for targeting telecommunications. The ASD is actively notifying victims and collaborating with ISPs to mitigate the threat.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with reconnaissance to identify vulnerable devices, followed by weaponization through the development of the BadCandy webshell. Delivery occurs via exploitation of the CVE-2023-20198 vulnerability, allowing installation of the webshell. Command and control is maintained through remote execution capabilities, and actions on objectives involve executing commands with root privileges. The attack highlights the importance of patching and monitoring to prevent exploitation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the BadCandy webshell as a tool, the CVE-2023-20198 vulnerability as a TTP, and the use of HTTP for command and control. The lack of specific IP addresses or domain names in the available data limits the ability to target specific indicators. The focus should be on detecting the use of the webshell and monitoring for exploitation attempts against the known vulnerability.

Title: Exploitation of CVE-2025-11833 in Post SMTP Plugin on WordPress Sites

Victim.Description: WordPress sites using Post SMTP plugin versions 3.6.0 and older.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves threat actors exploiting CVE-2025-11833 in the Post SMTP plugin on WordPress sites. The adversary's capability includes exploiting a critical vulnerability to gain unauthorized access to email logs and hijack administrator accounts. The infrastructure affected includes WordPress sites using vulnerable versions of the plugin. Victims are primarily WordPress site administrators, with the potential for full site compromise.
doc_summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical vulnerability, CVE-2025-11833, in the Post SMTP plugin on WordPress sites, affecting over 400,000 installations. The flaw allows unauthorized access to email logs, enabling attackers to hijack administrator accounts by intercepting password reset emails. Wordfence confirmed the exploit and disclosed it to the vendor, Saad Iqbal. A patch was released on October 29, 2025, but many sites remain vulnerable. The vulnerability stems from missing authorization checks in the PostmanEmailLogs constructor, allowing unauthenticated access to sensitive email content. Exploitation began on November 1, 2025, with over 4,500 attempts blocked by Wordfence.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance, where attackers identify WordPress sites using the vulnerable Post SMTP plugin. Exploitation occurs through CVE-2025-11833, allowing unauthorized access to email logs and administrator account takeover. Actions on objectives include hijacking admin accounts and potentially compromising entire sites. Detection involves monitoring for unauthorized access and unusual admin activity, while remediation includes updating the plugin to version 3.6.1.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the exploitation of CVE-2025-11833, a critical vulnerability in the Post SMTP plugin. No specific hashes, IP addresses, or domains were identified, but the TTPs involve exploiting a public-facing application vulnerability. The primary tool is the vulnerable plugin itself, and the main IOC is the CVE identifier. Detection and remediation focus on monitoring access and updating the plugin.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves threat actors exploiting a critical remote command execution vulnerability in CentOS Web Panel (CWP). The adversary's capability includes leveraging shell injection techniques to execute arbitrary commands. The infrastructure targeted is primarily CWP instances used by web hosting providers and system administrators. The victims are those using vulnerable versions of CWP, with a critical impact severity due to potential unauthorized access and control over server assets.
doc_summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warns of a critical remote command execution flaw in CentOS Web Panel (CWP), exploited by threat actors. The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary shell commands. CWP is a Linux server management tool, widely used by web hosting providers. The flaw impacts all CWP versions before 0.9.8.1204 and was demonstrated by security researcher Maxime Rinaudo. The root cause is the file-manager endpoint processing requests without a per-user identifier, allowing shell injection. A fix was released on June 18, 2023, in version 0.9.8.1205. CISA added this to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, urging federal entities to apply updates by November 25, 2023. The agency also added CVE-2025-11371, a local file inclusion flaw in Gladinet CentreStack and Triofox products.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for this incident involves the exploitation of a vulnerability in CentOS Web Panel, allowing threat actors to gain initial access through remote command execution. Detection involves monitoring for unusual shell activity and network anomalies, while remediation includes applying security updates and implementing network segmentation.

doc_summary: In August 2023, the State of Nevada experienced a ransomware attack impacting over 60 government agencies. The breach began with a trojanized system administration tool downloaded by a state employee, leading to persistent access for threat actors. Symantec Endpoint Protection identified the malicious tool, but persistence mechanisms allowed continued access. The attackers installed remote-monitoring software, used encrypted network tunnels, and accessed critical servers, including a password vault. They deleted backup volumes and deployed ransomware on virtual machines. The state recovered 90% of data without paying ransom, incurring $259,000 in overtime costs and $1.3 million in vendor support. The incident highlighted Nevada's cyber resilience and transparency, with improvements in cybersecurity defenses following the attack.

Command and control were maintained using encrypted tunnels, and the adversary achieved their objectives by deploying ransomware and deleting backups.

Title: Cyber Attacks on Moldova's Central Election Commission

diamond_model_summary: The cyber attack on Moldova's Central Election Commission during the September 2025 elections was a coordinated effort to disrupt election processes and public information channels. doc_summary: Moldova's Central Election Commission (CEC) faced significant cyber attacks during the country's Parliament election on September 28, 2025. The attacks included high-volume DDoS attacks aimed at disrupting official election processes and public information channels. Cloudflare mitigated over 898 million malicious requests directed at the CEC within a 12-hour period. The attack patterns suggested a coordinated effort targeting election-related, civil society, and news websites. This incident highlights the increasing threat of cyber attacks on election infrastructure and the importance of robust cybersecurity measures to protect democratic processes.

doc_summary: SonicWall, a cybersecurity company, reported a security breach in September 2023 involving unauthorized access to firewall configuration backup files. The breach was attributed to state-sponsored threat actors who accessed cloud backup files using an API call. The incident affected less than 5% of SonicWall's customers and did not impact its products, firmware, or other systems. SonicWall engaged Mandiant, a Google-owned company, to investigate the breach and has implemented remedial actions to strengthen its network and cloud infrastructure. The company advised customers to check their devices and reset credentials for impacted services. SonicWall released tools for online analysis and credential reset to assist customers in remediation efforts. The breach is unrelated to ongoing global Akira ransomware attacks.

Title: Curly COMrades Exploit Virtualization to Deploy Custom Malware

Victim.Description: Targets include entities in Georgia and Moldova.

diamond_model_summary: Curly COMrades is a sophisticated threat actor exploiting virtualization technologies to deploy custom malware. They have been active since late 2023, targeting Georgia and Moldova with interests aligned with Russia. Their capabilities include using Hyper-V to create a hidden VM environment, deploying tools like CurlyShell and CurlCat for reverse shell and proxy operations. The infrastructure involves using HTTP and SSH for C2 communication, while victims are primarily Windows 10 hosts in Georgia and Moldova.
doc_summary: The threat actor Curly COMrades has been exploiting virtualization technologies to bypass security solutions and execute custom malware. Bitdefender reports that the adversary enabled Hyper-V on victim systems to deploy an Alpine Linux-based VM hosting CurlyShell and CurlCat. First documented in August 2025, the group targets Georgia and Moldova, aligning with Russian interests. Tools like CurlCat, RuRat, Mimikatz, and MucorAgent were used. Collaboration with Georgia CERT revealed additional tooling and long-term access attempts via Hyper-V on Windows 10. The malware, written in C++, connects to a C2 server using HTTP requests. CurlyShell and CurlCat share a code base but differ in data handling. The group uses Resocks, Rsockstun, Ligolo-ng, CCProxy, Stunnel, and SSH for proxy and tunneling.
kill_chain_summary: The attack by Curly COMrades follows a structured kill chain. Initially, they exploit Hyper-V to gain initial access and create a hidden VM environment. Custom malware like CurlyShell and CurlCat is weaponized and delivered within this environment. The installation phase involves setting up persistence mechanisms using Windows services. Command and control are established via HTTP and SSH, allowing the execution of commands and data exfiltration. The attackers employ defensive evasion tactics by isolating malware within a VM, bypassing traditional EDR detections.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes several indicators. Hash values of the custom malware CurlyShell and CurlCat are critical for detection. IP addresses and domain names used for C2 communication are also significant. Network host artifacts include the use of Hyper-V and Alpine Linux VMs. Tools like Mimikatz and RuRat are employed for credential harvesting and remote access. TTPs involve virtualization exploitation and reverse shell deployment, making detection challenging.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified vulnerabilities in OpenAI's ChatGPT models, specifically GPT-4o and GPT-5, which can be exploited through indirect prompt injection attacks. These vulnerabilities allow attackers to manipulate the AI's behavior and exfiltrate user data. Tenable researchers Moshe Bernstein and Liv Matan highlighted the risks of exposing AI chatbots to external tools, increasing the attack surface. The vulnerabilities also relate to the broader issue of AI models being trained on contaminated data, leading to potential 'brain rot'. Studies from Anthropic and other institutions have shown that AI models can be backdoored with minimal poisoned data, challenging previous assumptions about the scale of data needed for such attacks. The research underscores the need for robust safety mechanisms in AI systems to prevent malicious exploitation.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with reconnaissance to identify vulnerabilities in AI models, followed by weaponization through crafting malicious prompts. Delivery involves injecting these prompts into the AI model, leading to exploitation where the AI performs unintended actions. The final stage, actions on objectives, involves exfiltrating data and manipulating AI outputs.

Title: PROMPTFLUX: AI-Driven VB Script Malware Leveraging Gemini API for Obfuscation

Victim.Description: The malware targets a wide range of users without specific industry or geographic focus.

diamond_model_summary: The PROMPTFLUX incident involves an unknown threat actor using AI-driven VB Script malware to evade detection. The malware interacts with the Gemini AI model API for code obfuscation, indicating a high level of sophistication. The actor's motivation appears to be financial, with a broad targeting approach. The infrastructure includes the use of a hard-coded API key for communication with the Gemini API. The victim profile is wide-ranging, with no specific industry or geographic focus.
doc_summary: Google discovered a threat actor using PROMPTFLUX, a VB Script malware, interacting with Gemini AI model API for code obfuscation and evasion. The malware uses a hard-coded API key to query Gemini for VB Script changes, aiming to evade antivirus detection. PROMPTFLUX saves obfuscated versions to Windows Startup for persistence and attempts propagation via removable drives and network shares. Despite its self-modification function being commented out, the malware logs AI responses, indicating a goal of creating a metamorphic script. The malware is under development, lacking means to compromise networks or devices. Security researcher Marcus Hutchins criticized the AI's role, noting the absence of entropy and functional guardrails. Google observed other LLM-powered malware and AI abuse by state-sponsored actors for phishing, C2 development, and data exfiltration. The increasing use of AI in cyber operations is expected to enhance attack speed and scope.
kill_chain_summary: The PROMPTFLUX malware follows a sophisticated kill chain involving AI-driven obfuscation and evasion techniques. The weaponization stage involves developing capabilities to use AI for code obfuscation. Delivery is attempted through removable drives and network shares. Installation is achieved by saving obfuscated versions to the Windows Startup folder for persistence. Command and Control is maintained through interaction with the Gemini API. The malware is still under development, lacking exploitation and actions on objectives stages.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The PROMPTFLUX incident highlights the use of AI-driven obfuscation techniques, making traditional detection methods challenging. The absence of specific indicators like hashes, IPs, or domains in the report limits the ability to apply the Pyramid of Pain effectively. The focus on AI and dynamic code generation suggests a shift towards more sophisticated evasion tactics, complicating detection and response efforts. This summary underscores the evolving nature of threats leveraging AI technologies.

doc_summary: Cisco disclosed new attack variants targeting devices running Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD Software, exploiting CVE-2025-20333 and CVE-2025-20362. These vulnerabilities, disclosed in September 2025, were exploited as zero-day vulnerabilities to deliver malware like RayInitiator and LINE VIPER. CVE-2025-20333 allows arbitrary code execution as root, while CVE-2025-20362 enables access to restricted URLs without authentication. Cisco also addressed critical flaws in Unified Contact Center Express and a high-severity DoS bug in Identity Services Engine. The U.K. National Cyber Security Centre reported these vulnerabilities, and security researcher Jahmel Harris was credited for their discovery.

The adversary gains initial access by exploiting CVE-2025-20333 and CVE-2025-20362, allowing them to execute arbitrary code and access restricted URLs. Detection and remediation efforts should focus on monitoring for unusual HTTP requests and applying Cisco's security updates to mitigate the vulnerabilities.

Title: InedibleOchotense Phishing Campaign Impersonating ESET Targeting Ukraine

Victim.Description: Ukrainian entities targeted by phishing campaigns impersonating ESET.

diamond_model_summary: The InedibleOchotense campaign involved a Russia-aligned adversary targeting Ukrainian entities by impersonating ESET. The capability included spear-phishing emails and Signal messages delivering a trojanized installer with the Kalambur backdoor. The infrastructure utilized domains mimicking ESET, and the victims were various sectors in Ukraine. The campaign aimed to exfiltrate data and enable remote access, highlighting the ongoing threat from Russia-aligned actors.
doc_summary: In May 2025, a phishing campaign by the Russia-aligned group InedibleOchotense targeted Ukrainian entities by impersonating ESET. The campaign involved spear-phishing emails and Signal messages with links to a trojanized ESET installer. The installer delivered a C# backdoor named Kalambur, using the Tor network for command-and-control, and enabled remote access via RDP. The campaign shared tactics with previous operations involving the BACKORDER backdoor and was linked to Sandworm sub-clusters UAC-0212 and UAC-0125. Domains used included esetsmart.com, esetscanner.com, and esetremover.com. CERT-UA and ESET reported on the campaign, highlighting the ongoing threat from Russia-aligned actors in Ukraine.
kill_chain_summary: The InedibleOchotense campaign followed a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance on Ukrainian entities using ESET software. Weaponization involved creating a trojanized installer, followed by delivery through spear-phishing emails and Signal messages. Installation of the Kalambur backdoor enabled command-and-control via the Tor network. The campaign's objectives included data exfiltration and remote access via RDP, demonstrating a sophisticated and targeted approach.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for the InedibleOchotense campaign includes domain names like esetsmart.com, tools such as Kalambur and Tor, and TTPs involving phishing and impersonation. These indicators highlight the adversary's reliance on specific infrastructure and techniques, making detection and disruption challenging. The campaign's use of legitimate software for malicious purposes further complicates defensive efforts, emphasizing the need for robust monitoring and analysis.

diamond_model_summary: The Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters (SLH) collective, formed by Scattered Spider, LAPSUS$, and ShinyHunters, is involved in extortion and ransomware operations. They use Telegram for coordination and dissemination, and are developing the Sh1nySp1d3r ransomware. SLH is part of The Com, a federated cybercriminal enterprise, and collaborates with groups like DragonForce. Their operations blend financially motivated cybercrime with hacktivism, using social engineering and remote access tools to gain initial access.
doc_summary: The nascent collective Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters (SLH), formed by Scattered Spider, LAPSUS$, and ShinyHunters, has been active since August 2025, creating 16 Telegram channels for coordination. SLH engages in data extortion attacks, offering extortion-as-a-service (EaaS) to affiliates. The group is part of The Com, a federated cybercriminal enterprise, and has ties with CryptoChameleon and Crimson Collective. SLH uses Telegram to disseminate messages and market services, accusing Chinese state actors of exploiting vulnerabilities and targeting U.S. and U.K. law enforcement. Known members include Rey, SLSHsupport, and yuka, an initial access broker. SLH hints at developing Sh1nySp1d3r ransomware to rival LockBit and DragonForce. DragonForce, aligned with Scattered Spider, uses BYOVD attacks with vulnerable drivers like truesight.sys. Title: Analysis of BankBot-YNRK and DeliveryRAT Android Trojans

Victim.Description: Victims are Android device users, particularly those using versions 13 and below, targeted for financial data theft.
Victim.Security_Posture: Vulnerable to Android versions 13 and below

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves two Android trojans, BankBot-YNRK and DeliveryRAT, targeting financial data and executing fraudulent transactions. The adversaries use evasion techniques and target specific Android devices. The infrastructure includes remote servers for command and control, and the victims are Android users, particularly in the Russian Federation.
doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers have identified two Android trojans, BankBot-YNRK and DeliveryRAT, capable of harvesting sensitive data from compromised devices. BankBot-YNRK evades detection by checking for virtualized environments and targets specific devices like Google Pixel and Samsung. It impersonates the Indonesian government app Identitas Kependudukan Digital and uses Android's JobScheduler for persistence. DeliveryRAT targets Russian Android users, distributed via a Telegram bot under a malware-as-a-service model. It hides its icon and accesses SMS and call logs. Both malware families exploit Android versions 13 and below, with BankBot-YNRK leveraging accessibility services for privilege escalation. The discovery coincides with a report of 760 Android apps misusing NFC to steal payment data.
kill_chain_summary: The attack involves delivery of malware via APK files, exploitation of Android devices running versions 13 and below, installation for persistence, command and control communication with remote servers, and actions on objectives such as data theft and fraudulent transactions. The malware uses Android's JobScheduler for persistence and exploits accessibility services for privilege escalation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes domain names like ping.ynrkone.top, which are critical for command and control. The malware families BankBot-YNRK and DeliveryRAT are tools used by the adversaries. The attack techniques involve exploiting Android vulnerabilities and using accessibility services for privilege escalation.

Title: Exploitation of CVE-2023-20198 in Cisco IOS XE Devices by China-linked Salt Typhoon

Victim.Description: Telecommunications providers in Australia targeted by Salt Typhoon.

diamond_model_summary: The incident involves China-linked threat actors, Salt Typhoon, exploiting a critical vulnerability, CVE-2023-20198, in Cisco IOS XE devices. The adversary uses the BADCANDY web shell to compromise telecommunications infrastructure in Australia. The lack of persistence in the malware allows for re-exploitation if devices remain unpatched.
doc_summary: The Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) has issued a bulletin regarding ongoing cyber attacks targeting unpatched Cisco IOS XE devices in Australia. The attacks involve the exploitation of CVE-2023-20198, a critical vulnerability with a CVSS score of 10.0, allowing remote attackers to create accounts with elevated privileges. The vulnerability has been actively exploited by China-linked threat actors, specifically Salt Typhoon, to breach telecommunications providers. The malware used, BADCANDY, is a Lua-based web shell that lacks persistence but can be reintroduced if devices remain unpatched. As of October 2025, 400 devices have been compromised, with 150 infections occurring in October alone. The ASD emphasizes the importance of applying patches and limiting public exposure to prevent further exploitation.
kill_chain_summary: The attack begins with the exploitation of CVE-2023-20198, allowing unauthorized access to Cisco IOS XE devices. The BADCANDY web shell is installed, providing a foothold for the adversary. The lack of persistence means the malware can be reintroduced if devices are not patched, highlighting the importance of timely remediation.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the BADCANDY web shell as a tool and the exploitation of CVE-2023-20198 as a TTP. The lack of specific IP addresses or domain names limits the ability to track the adversary's infrastructure. The focus should be on detecting the web shell and applying patches to mitigate the threat.

Title: University of Pennsylvania Email Breach Incident

diamond_model_summary: The incident at the University of Pennsylvania involved an unknown adversary sending offensive emails from compromised University email addresses. The adversary's motivation appears to be ideological, aiming to discredit the University's security practices and policies. The attack leveraged the University's email infrastructure, specifically the 'connect.upenn.edu' platform hosted on Salesforce Marketing Cloud. The victim, the University of Pennsylvania, is part of the education sector in the United States, with email systems being the primary targeted asset. The impact severity is assessed as medium due to the potential reputational damage and exposure of email addresses.
doc_summary: The University of Pennsylvania experienced a cybersecurity incident involving the distribution of offensive emails to students and alumni. The emails, sent from various University email addresses, claimed data was stolen in a breach and criticized the University's security practices and policies. The emails were sent via the 'connect.upenn.edu' platform, hosted on Salesforce Marketing Cloud. The University's Incident Response team is addressing the breach, and a banner on the University's website advises recipients to disregard the emails. The incident highlights potential vulnerabilities in email systems and the importance of robust cybersecurity measures in higher education institutions.

The delivery stage involved sending offensive emails via the compromised 'connect.upenn.edu' platform. The actions on objectives stage aimed to discredit the University by spreading false and offensive messages. The adversary's tactics included phishing and defacement, with the goal of impacting the University's reputation. Detection measures should focus on monitoring email logs and content for unusual patterns, while remediation efforts should include strengthening email security policies and restoring affected systems from backups.

Title: Airstalk Malware Linked to Nation-State Supply Chain Attack

Victim.Description: Potential targets in the business process outsourcing sector.

diamond_model_summary: The Airstalk malware incident involves a suspected nation-state actor, identified as CL-STA-1009, targeting the business process outsourcing sector. The malware uses the AirWatch API for covert command-and-control communications, indicating a sophisticated supply chain attack. The adversary's motivation appears to be state-backed, with a focus on maintaining persistent access to compromised systems. The infrastructure leverages the AirWatch API, and the victim profile includes organizations in the BPO sector, highlighting the potential for significant data exposure.
doc_summary: Airstalk is a new malware linked to a suspected nation-state threat actor, identified by Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 as CL-STA-1009. The malware is part of a likely supply chain attack, misusing the AirWatch API for mobile device management, now called Workspace ONE Unified Endpoint Management, to establish a covert command-and-control channel. Airstalk appears in PowerShell and .NET variants, with the latter having more capabilities. It captures screenshots, harvests cookies, browser history, and bookmarks, and uses a stolen certificate for signing artifacts. The .NET variant targets Microsoft Edge and Island browsers, mimicking an AirWatch Helper utility. The malware uses the AirWatch MDM API for C2 communications, suggesting a supply chain attack targeting the business process outsourcing sector. The evasion techniques allow it to remain undetected, posing a significant risk to organizations using BPO services.
kill_chain_summary: The Airstalk malware attack follows a structured kill chain, beginning with the weaponization of the malware in PowerShell and .NET variants. The installation phase involves the use of scheduled tasks for persistence in the PowerShell variant. Command and control are achieved through the misuse of the AirWatch API, allowing for covert communications. The actions on objectives include data exfiltration and system manipulation, with the malware capable of capturing screenshots and harvesting browser data. The attack highlights the use of sophisticated evasion techniques, including the use of a stolen certificate.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Airstalk malware incident presents several indicators of compromise, including a file hash and the use of specific tools like PowerShell and .NET. The misuse of the AirWatch API for command-and-control communications is a key tactic, along with the use of a stolen certificate for evasion. These indicators provide varying levels of difficulty for detection and response, with the hash value being the easiest to detect and the TTPs employed by the adversary being the most challenging. The incident underscores the importance of monitoring for unusual API usage and certificate anomalies.

doc_summary: The cyber espionage group Tick, also known as Bronze Butler, has been exploiting a critical vulnerability CVE-2025-61932 in Motex Lanscope Endpoint Manager. This flaw allows remote attackers to execute commands with SYSTEM privileges. The group, suspected to be from China, has been active since 2006, targeting East Asia, particularly Japan. Sophos observed the use of the Gokcpdoor backdoor, which establishes a proxy connection and executes malicious commands. The attack also involved the Havoc post-exploitation framework, DLL side-loading, and tools like goddi for Active Directory information dumping. JPCERT/CC confirmed active abuse of this vulnerability, urging organizations to upgrade vulnerable Lanscope servers. The campaign highlights the use of cloud services for data exfiltration and the historical pattern of Tick leveraging zero-day vulnerabilities.
kill_chain_summary: The attack follows a structured kill chain, starting with the exploitation of CVE-2025-61932 for initial access. The Gokcpdoor backdoor is installed for persistence, and the smux protocol is used for command and control. The adversary conducts data exfiltration using cloud services, demonstrating a sophisticated approach to achieving their objectives.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for this incident includes the use of specific tools like Gokcpdoor and Havoc, and techniques such as DLL side-loading and smux protocol for C2. doc_summary: Near-Field Communication (NFC) relay malware has surged in Eastern Europe, with over 760 malicious Android apps discovered. These apps exploit Android's Host Card Emulation (HCE) to steal payment card information by capturing EMV fields and responding to APDU commands. The malware was first detected in Poland in 2023, followed by campaigns in the Czech Republic and Russia. Variants include data harvesters, relay toolkits, and ghost-tap payments. Zimperium identified over 70 command-and-control servers and app distribution hubs, with apps impersonating Google Pay and banks like Santander, VTB, and ING. Android users are advised to avoid installing APKs from untrusted sources and to disable NFC if not needed.

doc_summary: Google has implemented robust defenses in Android to protect users from over 10 billion suspected malicious calls and messages monthly. The company has blocked over 100 million suspicious numbers from using Rich Communication Services (RCS) to prevent scams. Google's analysis in August 2025 identified employment fraud as the most prevalent scam category, targeting individuals with fake job opportunities to steal personal and financial information. Other scams include unpaid bills, subscriptions, fraudulent investments, package deliveries, government impersonation, romance, and technical support scams. Scammers increasingly use group chats to make messages appear legitimate. The scam messages follow a distinct schedule, peaking on Mondays. Common tactics include 'Spray and Pray' and 'Bait and Wait,' aiming to steal information or money. Scammers use SIM farms, Phishing-as-a-Service kits, and bulk messaging services to distribute malicious links. The scam landscape is volatile, with scammers shifting operations as enforcement tightens.

doc_summary: A severe vulnerability named Brash was disclosed in the Chromium Blink rendering engine by security researcher Jose Pino. This vulnerability can crash Chromium-based browsers like Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave, Opera, and others within seconds by exploiting an architectural flaw in DOM operations. The flaw involves the lack of rate limiting on document.title API updates, allowing millions of DOM mutations per second, leading to browser crashes and degraded system performance. The attack can be programmed to execute at specific times, acting as a logic bomb. Mozilla Firefox and Apple Safari are immune. The Hacker News has reached out to Google for comments on a fix.

doc_summary: A phishing campaign targeting Colombian, Spanish-speaking individuals was observed between August and October 2025. The activity was reported by IBM X-Force, highlighting the evolving threat landscape and the use of novel techniques to target high-impact individuals.

doc_summary: Cybersecurity researchers discovered 10 malicious npm packages designed to deliver an information stealer targeting Windows, Linux, and macOS. The malware uses four layers of obfuscation, displays a fake CAPTCHA, fingerprints victims by IP address, and downloads a 24MB PyInstaller-packaged information stealer. The packages impersonate popular npm libraries like TypeScript, discord.js, ethers.js, nodemon, react-router-dom, and zustand. The malware captures the victim's IP address, sends it to an external server, and drops the main malware. The JavaScript payload is hidden through XOR cipher, URL-encoding, and hexadecimal and octal arithmetic. The stealer extracts credentials from system keyrings using the keyring npm library, compresses the data into a ZIP archive, and exfiltrates it to the server.

Title: Operation ForumTroll: Exploitation of CVE-2025-2783 in Google Chrome

Victim.Description: The campaign targeted Russian organizations across various sectors.

diamond_model_summary: Operation ForumTroll involved a sophisticated adversary exploiting a zero-day vulnerability in Google Chrome to deliver espionage tools. The adversary, known as ForumTroll APT, targeted Russian organizations across multiple sectors. The campaign utilized spear-phishing emails to deliver the exploit, leading to the installation of the LeetAgent malware, which facilitated espionage activities.
doc_summary: The zero-day exploitation of CVE-2025-2783 in Google Chrome led to the distribution of espionage tools by Memento Labs, targeting organizations in Russia. The campaign, known as Operation ForumTroll, involved phishing emails with links to the Primakov Readings forum, exploiting the vulnerability to deliver the LeetAgent spyware. Memento Labs, formed from InTheCyber Group and HackingTeam, has a history of selling offensive capabilities. The attacks targeted media, universities, and government bodies, with connections to the TaxOff/Team 46 and Prosperous Werewolf clusters. The LeetAgent backdoor facilitated the deployment of the Dante spyware, known for its obfuscation and anti-analysis features. The campaign highlights the sophistication and targeted nature of the threat actors involved.
kill_chain_summary: The kill chain for Operation ForumTroll began with reconnaissance to identify targets, followed by weaponization of the CVE-2025-2783 exploit. Delivery was achieved through spear-phishing emails containing malicious links. Exploitation of the vulnerability allowed for sandbox escape and installation of the LeetAgent malware. Command and control was established via HTTPS, enabling espionage activities on compromised systems.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The Pyramid of Pain for Operation ForumTroll includes several indicators: the use of the LeetAgent and Dante malware, the CVE-2025-2783 exploit, and HTTPS-based C2 communication. These indicators highlight the sophistication and targeted nature of the campaign, with a focus on espionage activities against Russian organizations.

Title: SideWinder Campaign Targets South Asian Diplomatic Entities

Victim.Description: Diplomatic entities in South Asia, including a European embassy in New Delhi.

diamond_model_summary: The SideWinder campaign in 2025 targeted diplomatic entities in South Asia, using spear-phishing emails with malicious PDF and Word documents. The adversary employed sophisticated techniques, including ClickOnce-based infection chains and DLL sideloading, to deploy custom malware like ModuleInstaller and StealerBot. The infrastructure involved domains mimicking government entities, and the campaign demonstrated a high level of sophistication and geopolitical awareness.
doc_summary: SideWinder, a threat actor, targeted a European embassy in New Delhi and organizations in Sri Lanka, Pakistan, and Bangladesh in 2025. The campaign involved spear-phishing emails with PDF and Word documents exploiting Microsoft Office flaws. The infection chain used ClickOnce applications to sideload malicious DLLs, deploying ModuleInstaller and StealerBot malware. These tools gathered sensitive data, including screenshots and keystrokes. The attacks demonstrated SideWinder's sophisticated evasion techniques and geopolitical awareness. The campaign's infrastructure included domains like mod.gov.bd.pk-mail.org and mofa-gov-bd.filenest.live, with region-locked C2 communications.
kill_chain_summary: The SideWinder campaign followed a structured kill chain, starting with reconnaissance to craft targeted spear-phishing emails. Weaponization involved exploiting Microsoft Office vulnerabilities in PDF and Word documents. Delivery was achieved through spear-phishing emails, leading to exploitation and installation of malware. Command and control were maintained via region-locked communications, and actions on objectives included data collection from compromised hosts.
pyramid_of_pain_summary: The SideWinder campaign's pyramid of pain includes domain names like mod.gov.bd.pk-mail.org and mofa-gov-bd.filenest.live, which are critical for detection. The campaign's sophisticated TTPs, including DLL sideloading and region-locked C2 communications, present significant challenges for defenders.
